title: Concordance router: adaptive regional dispatch with latency budgets and capacity escrow
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Problem:
Currently regional routing mixes latency-preferring and capacity-preferring signals but lacks a single coherent policy for: (1) preserving P95/P99 latency SLOs for pinned customers, (2) gracefully shedding load under cross-region saturation, and (3) avoiding cascading capacity failures when a region transitions to transient overload.

Goal:
Design and implement an 'Concordance Router' policy that: 1) attaches per-route latency budgets (absolute and relative) to inform hedging and pin fallback decisions; 2) tracks a capacity escrow credit per region to allow short-term burst absorbtion without full failover; 3) provides circuit-breaker hooks (soft and hard) for progressive shedding and deterministic fallbacks to compatible model variants/regions.

Non-goals:
- Replace all existing geo-routing implementations in one change. This is an incremental policy that plugs into the existing steering layer and the admission controller.

Acceptance criteria:
- New policy can be enabled per-customer or per-route via config flag in the control plane.
- For a synthetic workload test (described in test plan), Concordance Router maintains P95 latency within 1.2x baseline under 20% cross-region load surge while reducing cross-region ejections vs current policy by >= 30%.
- On region saturation, capacity escrow prevents immediate full regional failover for at least 30s of burst traffic, with graceful progressive shedding afterwards.
- Circuit-breaker state transitions are instrumented and visible in Console runbooks/dashboards.

Proposed design (high-level):
- Latency budgets: config per-route with two values: baseline_latency_ms and budget_multiplier. Router computes a real-time effective deadline for a request and prefers local/fast routes when within budget.
- Capacity escrow: each region accrues an escrow credit proportional to spare capacity and recent healthy throughput; credits can be consumed by short bursts and are replenished by autoscaler events and steady-state headroom.
- Steering decision matrix: combine latency budget pressure, escrow availability, and SLO-penalty score (derived from token-weighted SLO impact) to produce a ranked list of candidate targets.
- Circuit breaker: two-tier CB: soft CB triggers proportional shedding (10/30/50%) with preference for non-pinned customers; hard CB trips full routing restriction and immediate rollout to fallback model/region.
- Observability: add traces, per-request decision tags, and a Concordance Router dashboard with heatmaps for escrow consumption, CB state, and latency budget violations.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs transparency: richer scoring improves decisions but increases surface area for bugs. We keep scoring linear and deterministic with a single tunable weight set.
- Escrow size vs safety: large escrows reduce false failovers but risk masking real capacity shortages. We opt for conservative escrow caps (configurable per-tenant).
- Pinning fidelity: strict pinning preserves data locality but may harm latency under heavy load; policy allows configurable pin looseness windows for emergency shedding.

Rollout plan:
1) Simulate policy in canary environment against replayed production traces (2 weeks).
2) Launch on small set of non-critical customers with detailed telemetry.
3) Expand with staged percentage rollout and automatic rollback if P99 regressions exceed threshold.

Dependencies and follow-ups:
- Integrate with admission controller quota signals (ENG-21057).
- Console dashboard work and alerting (follow-up ticket: PM/Console collaboration).
- Eval harness updates to include a stress scenario with bursty multi-region traffic.
updates: 2026-02-25 - Ticket created by Aisha Gupta with initial design intent and acceptance criteria. Linked to ENG-21057 for admission controller signal dependency.

2026-03-01 - Spike completed: microsim of scoring algorithm (Python notebook) shows deterministic ranking reduces poor failovers in replay test by ~22%. Notebook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-simulations/tree/main/concordance-spike

2026-03-03 - Design review with Platform/Serving teams. Feedback: prefer escrow replenishment tie to autoscaler window and add explicit max-escrow per-region. Action: add max_escrow param and document autoscaler signal mapping (see design doc).

2026-03-05 - Design doc posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Concordance+Router+-+Design. Reviewers: Marco Alvarez, Priya Nair, Tom Becker. Requested more observability hooks for debugging transient decisions. Added per-request decision tags and a debug sampling mode.

2026-03-07 - Prototype PR opened (serving-routing): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-routing/pull/412. PR implements scoring layer and soft CB stubs. Benchmarks included in PR description.

2026-03-09 - Bench results from canary replay: under 20% surge, P95 increased 1.15x baseline; cross-region ejection rate reduced 34%. Metrics dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/RegionalRouting/concordance-canary

2026-03-10 - Security review triage: security flagged that escrow credits could allow tenant spikes to bypass tenant-level quotas; agreed mitigation: escrow consumption requires quota token check and will decrement a quota bucket (implemented in PR #412).

2026-03-11 - PM review (Priya Nair): requested ability to opt-in per-route via control plane flag and a clear failure-mode notice in Console. Added 'concordance_enabled' flag and UI copy draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/concordance-router

2026-03-12 - Next steps: address PR feedback (fine-tune soft-shed percentages, add end-to-end test that triggers hard CB), coordinate with Console for rollout toggle, schedule integrated canary for 2026-03-18. Assigned follow-ups: Marco to finish PR, Tom to add dashboard panels, Aisha to own release notes and runbook.
Links to incident learnings referenced: incident-2025-11-region-ejection-analysis (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2025-11-Regional+Ejection+Analysis
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for scoring math and deterministic ordering. 2) End-to-end integration test: synthetic client that emits mixed pinned and non-pinned requests with burst pattern; assert escrow consumption, soft CB progression, and final hard CB behavior. 3) Replay canary with 7-day production traces, compare P95/P99, ejection counts, and cross-region traffic delta. 4) Chaos test: transient region slowdown; assert graceful shedding and no cascading failovers.
notes: Keep scoring weights conservative in initial rollout: weight_latency=1.0, weight_escrow=0.8, weight_slo_penalty=1.2. These will be tuned from canary telemetry. Ensure all state transitions emit events to the tracing pipeline for retrospective debugging.
